questions.title: What a Class Contains
questions.description: A class in Java is primarily a container for:
questions.Option1: Only import statements and package declarations
questions.Option2: Fields (data) and methods (behavior) that describe one kind of thing
questions.Option4: Only executable statements that run top to bottom like a script

questions.title: One Public Class Per File
questions.description: A single .java source file may contain:
questions.Option2: Exactly one class, which must be public
questions.Option3: Many classes, but at most one of them can be public

questions.title: Private Access Scope
questions.description: A field declared private in a class can be accessed directly:
questions.Option1: Only by code written inside that same class
questions.Option2: By any class in the same project
questions.Option3: By any class in the same package
questions.Option4: Only by subclasses of that class

questions.title: Default Visibility of Members
questions.description: A class member declared with no access modifier at all (default access) is visible:
questions.Option3: Only inside subclasses in any package
questions.Option4: To all classes in the same package

questions.title: Instantiation Meaning
questions.description: Object instantiation is the process of:
questions.Option1: Defining the fields of a class
questions.Option2: Creating a real object in memory from a class using the new keyword
questions.Option3: Renaming a class before compiling it

questions.title: Uninitialized Field Defaults
questions.description: The class Demo has four fields that are never explicitly initialized. What does this program print?
questions.Option3: Garbage values that differ on every run
questions.Option4: It fails to compile because the fields are not initialized

questions.title: Field versus Method Role
questions.description: Inside a class, the difference between a field and a method is:
questions.Option1: A method stores data for later; a field performs an action
questions.Option2: They are two names for the same thing
questions.Option3: A field stores a value (state); a method defines an action (behavior)
questions.Option4: Fields can only be used inside static methods

questions.title: Void Return Meaning
questions.description: A method declared with the return type void:
questions.Option1: Returns the value 0 to the caller
questions.Option2: Returns an empty String to the caller

questions.title: Getters and Setters Purpose
questions.description: Getters and setters are mainly used to:
questions.Option1: Replace the need for a main method
questions.Option2: Give outside code controlled access to private fields, with checks if needed
questions.Option4: Speed up arithmetic inside the class
